Use `Table(..., table=True)` for a styled table with `caption`, `thead`,
`tbody`, and `tfoot`. `DataTable` wraps that table in a bordered, raised
frame (`[table-frame]`). Inside `DataTable`, cells stay on one line and
the frame scrolls horizontally when the table is wider than its parent
container.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from answerui.demo import demo
from fastcore.test import *
```

## Tables

When you pass `table=True` to `Table`, `thead th` and `tfoot th` are
semibold (`--weight1`), with horizontal borders under the header and
between body and footer rows. Any `caption` appears below the table in
muted `--text-1` text. Add `num=True` to a `Th` or `Td` to align it to
the end with tabular digits (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`).
Inside `[prose]`, the prose stylesheet formats unmarked `table` elements
with `.875em` text and prose spacing.

`DataTable` wraps `Table(*c, table=True)` in a `Div` with
`table_frame=True` (`[table-frame]`). That container has a border, a
`--raised` shadow, `overflow-x: auto`, and `contain: inline-size`.
Because of `contain: inline-size`, a wide table scrolls inside the frame
rather than widening the page or its containing card. Inside
`[table-frame]`, `thead th` has a `--color-surface` background and cells
stay on one line (`white-space: nowrap`). Keyword attributes passed to
`DataTable` apply to the outer `Div`. For keyboard scrolling, pass
`role='region'`, `tabindex=0`, and `aria_label` on `DataTable`. Focused
frames show the `--ring` outline (`[table-frame]:focus-visible`).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### DataTable

``` python
def DataTable(

```

*A table in a bordered frame that scrolls when its contents are wider
than its container*

Here is a quarterly regional summary using `Caption`, `num=True` on
numeric cells, and totals in `Tfoot`:

``` python
DataTable.demo()
```

``` html

  <table table>
<caption>Revenue and average order in US$, Q3</caption>    <thead>

        <th>Region</th>
        <th num>Orders</th>
        <th num>Revenue</th>
        <th num>Average</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>North</td>
        <td num>1,204</td>
        <td num>38,410</td>
        <td num>31.90</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>South</td>
        <td num>862</td>
        <td num>27,955</td>
        <td num>32.43</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>West</td>
        <td num>1,531</td>
        <td num>50,112</td>
        <td num>32.73</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot>
      <tr>
        <th>Total</th>

</div>
```
